t: This is the Admiral Hardy, a pub in Greenwich, named for Sir Thomas Masterman Hardy. Hardy was a Royal Navy officer who fought in the French Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars, at Cape St. Vincent, the Nile and Copenhagen. He was flag captain to Lord Nelson and commanded HMS Victory at Trafalgar in 1805. Nelson was shot as he paced the deck with Hardy, and as he lay dying he spoke the famous words "Kiss me, Hardy." Hardy later became First Naval Lord, in November 1830. So the pub's name links this corner of Greenwich to Nelson's last moments.
